overview.oneLineTake: Yields gave stocks a break, but the AI trade just took a revenue hit, so tech-led downside and premium bids are the risk into Friday.
themes: AI revenue doubt hit the leaders: an FT report that OpenAI's annualised revenue is about $20B below what it signalled sank chips and AI infrastructure. QQQ closed at 747.58 (-1.34%), with MU -4.8%, AVGO -4.4%, ORCL -5.5% and NVDA -2.9%, while the Dow eked out a gain.
Bonds got a reprieve: the 10-year eased to about 5.23% after the 30-year auction cleared, even though its high yield was the highest since 2000.

Oil whipsawed: crude jumped on a fresh tanker attack and new Iran sanctions, then slipped below $90.50 after Trump ruled out Iran strikes before the midterms. Hurricane Isaias has Shell shutting in Gulf output.
Gold is bid again near $4,173 on lower yields and a softer dollar, and jobless claims stay near multi-decade lows.
AI financing stress is spreading: Firmus pulled its Nvidia-backed IPO, and AI debt is being repriced.
risks: A deeper AI repricing would hit a narrow, chip-led tape hardest, and VXN is already up to about 22.
Isaias damage or renewed Middle East attacks could push oil and inflation fears back up, putting the Fed's hike bias back in focus.
Deficit and long-end supply worries have not gone away, so yields can turn back up quickly.

nq.summary: NDX fell 1.4% after an FT report that OpenAI's annualised revenue is about $20B below what it signalled, which hit chips and AI infrastructure hardest. Yields eased after the 30-year auction cleared, so this was an AI problem, not a rates problem. NQ is bouncing modestly overnight. Thesis: mildly bearish, 5/10, sell rallies into resistance. Invalidation: NDX close above 31,125 or below 30,200. NDX levels: resistance 30,800, 30,985 (Thu open), 31,125 (Thu H); support 30,556 (Thu L), 30,400, 30,200.
nq.primaryCatalyst: Canada jobs at 7:30 PM BKK (forecast 6.1K, previous -41.7K), then UoM sentiment prelim at 9:00 PM BKK (forecast 47.5) and inflation expectations (previous 4.6%).
nq.primaryRisk: AI follow-through selling in NVDA/AVGO/ORCL/MU, Isaias damage, Iran headlines, or 10Y back above 5.35%.
nq.overnight: NQ up 0.3% inside a tight 30,953–31,087 band. Hang Seng Tech up about 2%, while China's STAR 50 fell about 3%. Firmus pulled its Nvidia-backed IPO. Gold ~$4,173, crude below $90.50.
nq.macro: 10Y eased to 5.23% even though the 30-year auction's high yield was the highest since 2000. Trump ruled out Iran strikes before the midterms, which cooled oil, but Hurricane Isaias has Shell shutting in Gulf output. Fed's Musalem said strong demand for capital, including AI, keeps rates higher than they used to be.
nq.volatility: VIX 15.4, VXN 22.0 (up 4.7%). The Nasdaq vol premium widened on the AI scare. Dealer gamma unavailable.

intelligence.summary: Almost €215 billion of French corporate bonds trade as safer than the government's, a near 18-fold jump this year. French 10-year OAT yield at 4.94%, up 8 bp.

intelligence.headline: Fed Minutes Show Hawkish Unity Behind September Rate Hike

intelligence.headline: Samsung Reaches New Profit Record With Memory Chip Windfall

intelligence.headline: AI Bubble Risks Worst S&P 500 Crash Since 2008, Strategist Says
intelligence.summary: Panmure Liberum's Joachim Klement sees a 36% S&P 500 drop by end-2027. Seven other strategists tracked by Bloomberg see 14% upside on average.

intelligence.headline: Robert Rubin Warns AI Boom Carries Risks for US Economy, Markets
intelligence.summary: Rubin flags cascading-failure risk if big AI firms or their borrowing suppliers can't meet commitments.

intelligence.headline: Nvidia-Backed IPO's Cratering Demand Sends AI Warning
